column1: Recovery Workbench process architecture: L1 processes
19 L1 processes in four layers. Counts are calculated from the L2 and L3 tabs. Modes are defined on the Key tab.

column4: Definition
Watch every performing and early-arrears account and decide whether, when and how to act before or at the first missed payment.
Reach the customer through the right channel at the right time, within contact limits and customer standards, and record the outcome.
Record each promise to pay, track it to the payment and move the case on when the promise is broken.
Raise the intensity of collection by senior phone contact, field visits or outside agencies when lighter treatment has failed.
Assess affordability, offer and book a restructure plan, and monitor it until the customer pays as agreed or the plan fails.

column3: Take over and own the case
column4: Take the case from collections at 90 days past due, with its history, and give it one owner and a running set of deadlines.
Value the case, decide the route, and resolve it with the customer by settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim or guarantor pursuit.
Take the case through notices, filing, judgment and enforcement until the debt is paid, settled or proven unrecoverable.
Take assets onto the books, hold them, and turn them into cash by auction or other routes, or sell the debt.

column3: Write off and recover after charge-off
column4: Write off the balance that cannot be recovered, post it, and keep recovering after charge-off until the case closes.
Answer customer contacts and handle the seven deviations that interrupt a decision, then return the case to the right decision.
Select, instruct, measure, pay and govern the partners who work cases for the bank, and end the contract when needed.
Read and file inbound documents, send letters and notices with proof of delivery, and keep documents and originals under control.

column3: Set strategy, policy and decision rules
column4: Set the segments, treatment policy, decision rules, limits, fees and the reference data every decision reads.
Report results, test strategies, monitor agents and models, keep data correct and feed what is learned back to policy.
column6: Recovery Workbench, data lake, Power BI

column4: Run quality assurance, conduct control, model and agent risk, audit response, access control, incidents and data subject rights.
Route every recommendation to the person with the authority to decide it, record one log entry per decision, and feed results back.
Forecast inflow, plan staff and partner capacity, and build and allocate the work lists that collectors and partners work from.
column6: Capacity model, dialer, field application, partner portal

column4: Receive payments from every channel, apply them to the right account and case, and reconcile cash to the case and the core.
